title: Workshop on “Building Your IoT Smart Clock”
text:
Programming and Electronics Beginner Workshop
Build Your IoT Smart Clock
Date: February 7
, 2024 (Wednesday)
Time: 2:00
– 5:00 pm
Venue: Makerspace A, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Kickstart your IoT journey and build a smart clock at this beginner-friendly workshop!
Learn IoT basics and assemble a smart clock that captures real-time data such as weather, news and social media updates. You may customize your device by programming dynamic responses such as color changes based on temperature. Take home a fully functional smart clock with IoT capabilities for further experimentation. Join now and explore more! Details of the workshop are as follows:
Date: February 7, 2024 (Wednesday)
Time: 2:00 – 5:00pm
Venue: Makerspace A, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Instructor: Mr Justus Ip, current undergraduate student from Department of Computer Science
Eligibility:
Priority to Innovation Wing members
. All HKU undergraduate students are welcome to join.
Quota: A limited quota of
25
will be offered on a first-come-first-served basis. No prior knowledge is required.
Syllabus
The following topics will be covered in the workshop:
C++ Programming Skills (Included in formal curriculum of Engineering)
For students with no prior knowledge of programming, a basic partially completed code will be provided. Basic programming techniques
will also be introduced,
such as if-statements, while statements, for-statements. Using the knowledge gained in the workshop, students will complete the provided code and bring their smart display to life.
For students with prior knowledge of programming, a more complex partially completed code will be provided. They will have to complete the code using advanced C++ concepts such as class, inheritance & pointers.
ESP32 Programming Skills
Students will learn how to program and connect the ESP32 to other components. They will need to properly wire the board and use the Arduino IDE to program the ESP32 using the ESP32 toolchain.
Adafruit NeoPixel, NeoMatrix, GFX Library & WS2812 Protocol
Students will learn how to use the famous Adafruit libraries, together with ESP32, to control the WS2812 LED matrix, in order to display different kinds of content.
Network Time Protocol (NTP)
Students will be provided with a code that uses NTP to display the current time. They will study the code and learn how to use NTP to obtain an accurate time from the internet.
IoT Knowledge, HTTP Rest API & JSON
Students with prior programming experience can take their IoT clock to the next level by customizing it to display information from various sources. For example, they can connect a stock API to display the instant price of a particular stock.

title: Workshop by UAS: From Ground to Air
text:
From Ground to Air
Drone Building and Programming Workshop for Beginners
by HKU UAS
Date:
November 6, 8, 9 & 11
, 2023 (Mon, Wed, Thu & Sat)
Time:
6:30 – 9:00pm (Weekdays); 10:00am -12:00nn (Sat)
Venue:
Open Event Area, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
HKUUAS aims to build a community of students who are interested in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and drone technology. In the training series, you will learn the scientific principle behind a quadcopter. You will also have the opportunity to practice piloting First-person view (FPV) drone and using ground control station software.
Objectives:
By the end of workshop, participants will be able to:
Gain basic understanding of current UAV technologies;
Learn basic techniques for piloting FPV drones;
Understand the control theory behind quadcopters and how to create one;
Identify quadcopter drone parts and their functions;
Utilize Ground Control Station (GCS) software; and
Learn about obstacle avoidance algorithms and their applications

title: Workshop by Quantum Education Society: Journey into the Quantum World
text:
Journey into the Quantum World
Hands-on Workshop on Superconductivity and Quantum Levitation
by Quantum Education Society
Date:
November 15
, 2023 (Wednesday)
Time:
2:00 – 4:00pm
Venue:
Thematic Workshop 3, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Quantum science explores the fascinating world of electrons, atoms, and molecules. It includes important concepts like wave-particle duality and entanglement, which develop into many path-breaking technologies such as quantum computing and superconductors.
In this workshop, some hands-on superconductivity demonstrations will be provided and their potential applications will be discussed. Students will get the opportunity to try out experiments like quantum levitation, which are used in high-speed trains such as the Maglev train in Shanghai.
Objectives:
By completing the workshop, participants will be able to:
Gain the concepts of Quantum mechanics with a hands-on demo kit;
Complete superconductivity and quantum levitation experiment;
Identify the electrical resistance of a superconductor;
Learn relationship of the magnetic forces between the superconductor and magnets; and
Distinguish between the Meissner effect and Flux pinning.

Mainland Study Tour
Prepare yourself for an incredible journey on the Mainland Study Tour, meticulously crafted to ignite your passion for advanced technology and fuel your innovative spirit. This exclusive tour is specifically designed for undergraduate students who have a strong desire to delve into groundbreaking technologies and discover new innovations.
From March 4 to 7, 2024, get ready to embark on a four-day expedition that will take you on immersive tours of renowned universities and cutting-edge companies and to gain valuable insights and knowledge along the way.

Selected participants will be notified via email. Please kindly respond to the email and settle full payment on or before the before the designated deadline.
Notes to participants:
Participants are required to travel and stay with the team throughout the study tour, unless otherwise advised by tour leaders.
No separate inbound and / or outbound travel arrangements will be entertained
.
Participants are responsible for their own visa and travel document application or renewal, as well as any personal expenses incurred during the Mainland study tour.
Participants are responsible for verifying whether they require a visa or Mainland Travel Permit for their travel and ensure a successful application before departure. Kindly note that the processing time for any visa applications to Mainland requires at least 14 days. Innovation Academy is not accountable for any losses incurred as a result of travel document-related issues leading to the inability to travel. Participants are advised to refer to the following webpage for detailed information regarding visa requirements for China:
https://www.visaforchina.cn/HKG2_EN/
Pre-trip briefing
All participants are required to attend the pre-trip briefing. It covers the details of the tour, reimbursement procedures and some key reminders.
Payment Arrangement
Participants must settle full payments of airfare and hotel accommodation directly to the travel agency on or before the designated date. Reimbursement will be made upon full attendance of all scheduled activities and submission of quality post-trip report.
Please note that no refund will be provided once the payment has been made. Innovation Academy does not handle any payment transactions in this regard.
Reimbursement Procedures
Participants will be able to reimburse up to a maximum 70% of total cost of eligible items at cost.
Participants submit reimbursement claim form together with all the necessary documents, including the boarding passes, to Innovation Academy.
Administration staff of Innovation Academy will process the application after receiving all the documents.
Finance and Enterprises Office of HKU will reimburse the eligible amount to participants according to their bank account information provided in the Student Information System (SIS) in HKU portal. The whole process may take up to three months.
Insurance
Travel insurance provided by HKU:
Participants should note that the University only provides standard travel insurance coverage for overseas trips or study abroad programmes approved/arranged by the University. Before leaving Hong Kong, students are strongly advised to arrange their own travel insurance to better suit their needs, especially if they are planning to travel beyond the official programme period for personal leisure purpose. If students require additional or special insurance coverage, they will need to make their own personal arrangements at their own expense. The travel insurance coverage arranged by the University could not be extended to cover personal needs or leisure travelling arrangements. Participants should refer to Cedars webpage

for more details.
Participants are advised to read through Travel Insurance Arrangement for Students
(Click to learn more)
and other related documents, such as 24/7 Global Travel Emergency Assistance Programme and the FAQ.

Present in a sharing session, if any, for Inno Wing members and other Engineering students at HKU on March 13, 2024 (Wednesday).
Upon the completion of the study tour, participants are required to submit a reflection report with not less than 500 words, together with a minimum of 3 good photos by March 22, 2024 (Friday).

text:
Pitching Workshop Series
Three workshops will be organized in January 2024 to equip students with essential soft skills that are practical in pitching, as well as in academic and at workplace.

Click here to watch the Briefing Session
Learn more about Pitch New Tech Ideas 2024

About the workshops
Three workshops will be organized in January to equip students with essential soft skills that are practical in pitching, as well as in academic and at workplace. All workshops have limited quotas and will be offered on a first-come-first-serve basis. All HKU undergraduate students are welcome to join,
with priority given to Innovation Wing members
. No prior knowledge is required.
Innovate and Elevate: How to Generate and Pitch Creative Ideas? (January 17, 2024)

Click the following links to learn about each workshop.
Innovate and Elevate: How to Generate and Pitch Creative Ideas?
Delivering Effective Presentation with Slide Deck and Video
Introduction to Proposal Writing
1st Workshop
Innovate and Elevate: How to Generate and Pitch Creative Ideas?
Join us in this workshop to unleash your creativity and enhance your pitching skills. We will explore the principles of innovation thinking, empowering you to think outside the box and generate fresh ideas. You will also learn how to solve problems practically using the Value Proposition Canvas framework. Additionally, the essential elements of an effective pitch will be covered, ensuring that your ideas are persuasive and impactful. Seize the opportunity to elevate your skills to the new heights. Details of the workshop are as follows:
Date: January 17, 2024 (Wednesday)
Time: 3:00 – 5:00pm (2 hours)
Venue: Brainstorming Area, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One
Instructor: Mr Michael Chik, Founder of Endamame AI, Ex-McKinsey Management Consultant
Quota: A limited quota of
40
will be offered on a first-come-first-served basis. No prior knowledge is required.

Introduction and Objectives (10 minutes)
Interactive Icebreaker (10 minutes)

Group Presentations and Feedback (15 minutes)
Break (5 min)

Introduction to Effective Pitching (10 minutes)
Group Activity: Crafting Your Elevator Pitch (10 minutes)
Pairing Activity: Pitch Practice (10 minutes)

Q&A & Summary of Key Takeaways (10 minutes)

Photo Gallery
To learn about other
pitching-related workshops

Delivering Effective Presentation with Slide Deck and Video
Visually captivating slide decks and videos enhance your presentations and convey your ideas effectively. In this workshop, you will learn techniques for creating compelling slide decks and videos, including tips for selecting the essential elements, slide deck creation and video editing. Additionally, you will be guided in creating a short video using the video editing software, OpenShot. Join this informative and practical workshop to elevate your presentation skills and take your presentations to the next level. Details of the workshop are as follows:

Instructor: Mr Kelvin Ip, Former Digital Content Creator of HKU Racing (Innovation Wing Affiliated SIG), Graduated in 2023

3rd Workshop
From Concept to Impact: Developing and Writing Convincing Proposal
Designed specifically for students who are new to proposal writing, this workshop is your gateway to mastering this essential skill, which helps you transform an idea into a convincing proposal. During the session, you will understand the purpose and structure of a proposal, as well as the key elements that make a proposal stand out. With exercises and practical examples, you will learn how to articulate your ideas persuasively. You are also welcome to bring along any proposals you are working on. Grab the opportunity to enhance your proposal writing abilities. Details of the workshop are as follows
Date: January 25, 2024 (Thursday)
Time: 2:00 – 3:30pm (1.5 hours)
Venue: Makerspace A, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One
Instructor: Professor May Chui, Associate Head of Innovation Academy, Faculty of Engineering, HKU
Quota: A limited quota of
30
will be offered on a first-come-first-served basis. No prior knowledge is required.
Tentative Rundown:
Part 1: Presentation – Mastering Proposal Writing (30 minutes)
Welcome and introduction to the workshop
Importance of proposal writing
Essential elements of a successful proposal
Recognizing common pitfalls and implementing improvement strategies in proposals
Methods for crafting a persuasive written pitch

Forming small teams and choosing a project idea from a pool of toy ideas or creating your own (5 minutes)
Small group sessions with a toy idea: devising an engaging project title (15 minutes)
Presentation: Volunteer groups share their project titles and receive feedback (10 minutes)
Small group sessions with a toy idea: formulating concise project objectives (15 minutes)
Presentation: Volunteer groups present their project objectives and receive feedback (10 minutes)
Q&A & Summary of Key Takeaways (5 minutes)

pitching-related workshops
About the Pitch New Tech Idea 2024
This contest allows HKU undergraduates to present their project ideas and recruit prospective teammates. The process helps to improve students’ ability to effectively advocate an idea or proposal to a large group of audience. It also provides an opportunity and flexibility for students to form their own team and grow their community of interest and passion.
By taking part in the pitching events, students can:
recruit prospective teammates to form student interest groups;
link up with Faculty Supervisors and Advisors;
improve your ability to effectively advocate an idea or proposal to a large group of audience;
receive suggestions on areas of improvement for strengthening your soft and technical skills;
gain support from Innovation Academy and Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing; and
obtain
a maximum of HK$100K funding support
to further develop the idea.

About HKU iGEM
HKU iGEM team is a team of undergraduate students from different fields, aiming at building safe and sustainable projects that serve the public interest. We participate in the International Genetically Engineered Machine Competition. We have chosen immunotherapy as our topic this year, tackling the obstacle of treating solid tumour with new approaches. Over years, HKU IGEM team have won multiple awards, welcoming students from different cohort, establish platforms of synthetic biology accessible for all students.
Workshop Details
Innovation Academy is thrilled to announce an exciting opportunity for all HKU students to join us for a fun-tastic adventure with HKU iGEM. The interesting hands-on bioinformatics activities will definitely provide you with a comprehensive understanding of iGEM and its gold-medal ideas. You will learn how they generate and translate their ideas into reality, as well as their future project planning. You are welcome to join their AI and algorithm project development too. title: Recruitment Workshop by HKU AI Smart Robotics Team: Unleashing the Power of AI and Robots
text:
Unleashing the Power of AI and Robots
Member Recruitment Workshop by HKU AI for Smart Robotics Team
Date:
January 30, 2024 (Tuesday)
Time:
1:00pm
– 2:00pm
Venue:
Makerspace A,
(Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One), Hui Oi Chow Science Building, HK
Registration
About HKU AI for Smart Robotics Team
Inspired by the remarkable dexterity of animals in nature and the large language models (LLM),
the HKU AI for Smart Robotics team
is committed to creating an intelligent robot system. Through collaborative work on real-world projects, we continuously accumulate valuable hands-on experience in the field of robotics. Our recent participation in the ICRA’s Robot Challenge, where we achieved third place in the manual category, standing alongside esteemed institutions such as MIT and CMU.
Currently, we are actively seeking like-minded Engineering undergraduates to join our team and contribute to our ambitious goals. If you share our passion and vision, we invite you to become a part of our dynamic team.
Workshop Details
Calling all robotic enthusiasts! The innovation Academy is excited to announce a golden opportunity for you to immerse yourself in a cultivating workshop by HKU AI for Smart Robotics Team. In this workshop, 5:
1. gain insights from their experience sharing on the design, control, and perception systems of their robots.
2. interact with their robots
3. join the team if you are interested.
Don’t miss out on this extraordinary opportunity! Come and join us to discover the limitless possibilities of robotics.
Date: January 30, 2024 (Tuesday)
Time: 1:00pm – 2:00pm
Venue: Brainstorming Area, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One
Eligibility: All Engineering undergraduates are welcome to join.
No prior knowledge is required.
Workshop Outline
Topics Included
Design and Production of Robots
Robot Control System Based on Reinforcement Learning
The Combination of Perception and Robot
Human-robot interaction with Robots
ICRA Robot Challenges
Question and Answer Session

The following
undergraduate
students are wanted. If you are interested, please send your
CV
to the email:
hkuai4robot@gmail.com
, with email subject
[AI for robots team – design/electrical/control/vision/speech – Your name]
1.
Design Group:
Mechanical design and build of quadruped robots.
Prior experience with SolidWorks, CAD software, mechanical design and build is a bonus.
2.
Electrical Group:
Development of motor control and microcontroller control systems.
Previous experience with motor control, microcontroller programming, specifically in C++, using Keil, and circuit design and manufacturing is a bonus.
3.
Control Group:
Quadruped robot’s whole body control, model predictive control and state estimation.
Prior experience with Automatic control theory and practice, motor or robot control, C++ or python is a bonus.
4.
Vision Group:
Development and deployment of sensing devices such as cameras and radars.
Prior experience with Computer Vision, Speech Recognition, SLAM is a bonus.
5.
Speech Group:
Development and application of human-computer interaction for robots. Familiar with Natural Language Processing and the Large Lagrange Model is a bonus.
But
what we highly value is an eagerness to learn.

Workshop Details
The Robot Operating System (ROS) (
https://www.ros.org/
) is a set of open-sourced software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms, and with powerful developer tools, ROS has what you need for your next robotics project. ROS is de facto industrial standard for developing system for robots. It is important to everyone who wants to work in the field of robotics.
This workshop consists of three sessions to lead beginners to learn ROS framework and e
ach session will take up 2 hours:

The Robot Operating System (ROS) ( https://www.ros.org/ ) is a set of open-sourced software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms, and with powerful developer tools, ROS has what you need for your next robotics project. ROS is de facto industrial standard for developing system for robots. It is important to everyone who wants to work in the field of robotics.
This workshop consists of three sessions to lead beginners to learn ROS framework and e ach session will take up 2 hours:
Date: February 19 (Mon), 22 (Thu) and 26 (Mon), 2024
Time: 2:30-4:30pm
Venue: Digital Learning Studio, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Instructor: Mr Henry Leung and Mr Johnson Zhang, Student Research Assistant of Innovation Wing
A limited quota of 18 will be offered on first-come-first-served basis.
Eligibility: All HKU Engineering Students and InnoHub members, preferably with C/C++ programming knowledge but not a must.

Date

Feb 19, 2024 (Monday)
Introduction to ROS What is ROS? Application of ROS How to access to ROS Structure of ROS
Session 2
Feb 22, 2024 (Thursday)

Session 3
Feb 26, 2024 (Monday)
ROS taster: Implementation and Control Experience initiation and linkage to Robot made by Interns Try out different control protocols through ROS

title: Recruitment Talk of InnoWing 2024 Summer Interns
text:
Recruitment Talk of 2024 Summer Student Research Assistant(s)
Date:
April 9, 2024 (Tuesday)
Time:
4:45-5:45pm
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register for The Talk
About the Recruitment Talk
Innovation Academy is looking for a new batch of Full-time Temporary Student Research Assistant(s) (SRA) for Summer 2024 in the following fields:
1. Robotics
2. Generative
3. Internet of Things
The Students Research Assistant(s) will participate in the application development projects in the respective areas with other academic disciplines or industry partners, as coordinated by the Innovation Academy. They will also involve in designing and delivering workshops.
In this recruitment talk, supervisors and the current SRAs of each stream will share about the internship experience, as well as their existing and upcoming projects.
Details
Innovation Academy is looking for a new group of Full-time Temporary Student Research Assistant(s) (SRAs) for Summer 2024 in the following fields:
1. Robotics
2. Generative AI
3. Internet of Things
The SRA(s) will participate in the application development projects in the respective areas with other academic disciplines or industry partners, as coordinated by the Innovation Academy. They will also involve in designing and delivering workshops.
During this recruitment talk, you will learn about the existing and upcoming projects, as well as the internship experience of the SRAs. Details of the talk are as follows:
Date:
April 9, 2024
(Tuesday)
Time:
4:45-5:45pm
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
All HKU students are welcome to join!
The appointment will commence from June to August 2024, with the possibility of part-time appointment in the next academic year, subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.
Project Directions
There are three main projects areas for our student research assistants:
Robotics:
motion planning and control, computer vision for robotics, and human-robot interface
Generative Artificial Intelligence:
LLM fine-tuning, AI agents, AI and robotics, computer vision, and story generation
Internet of Things:
wearable devices and devices for smart living, sensor networks, database, machine learning
To Apply for Student Research Assistants (SRAs)
Applicants must be current members of the Innovation Wing, with a strong background in coding, excellent written and spoken English skills, strong interpersonal and communication abilities, and exceptional presentation skills. They should demonstrate high levels of motivation, responsibility, and the ability to work independently, under pressure, and within tight deadlines. The role may require work outside of regular office hours.
The appointment will commence from June to August 2024, with the possibility of part-time appointment in the next academic year, subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.
We welcome undergraduates from all Faculties and MSc students to apply for this job.
Interested students can submit your application via
https://forms.gle/8FXtDJyk1C2BESQTA
with:
1. The latest CV (including the project(s) you have participated)
2. Purpose statement for this internship (within 300 words)
3. Preference on the projects – Robotics, Generative Artificial Intelligence and/or Internet of Things
4. The latest academic transcripts
5. The earliest available date
on or before April 12, 2024 (Monday)
. A confirmation email will be sent to you and an interview will be scheduled for shortlisted applicants.

The appointment will commence from June to August 2024, with the possibility of part-time appointment in the next academic year, subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.
There are three main projects areas for our student research assistants:
Robotics: motion planning and control, computer vision for robotics, and human-robot interface
Generative Artificial Intelligence: LLM fine-tuning, AI agents, AI and robotics, computer vision, and story generation
Internet of Things: wearable devices and devices for smart living, sensor networks, database, machine learning
Applicants must be current members of the Innovation Wing, with a strong background in coding, excellent written and spoken English skills, strong interpersonal and communication abilities, and exceptional presentation skills. They should demonstrate high levels of motivation, responsibility, and the ability to work independently, under pressure, and within tight deadlines. The role may require work outside of regular office hours.
The appointment will commence from June to August 2024, with the possibility of part-time appointment in the next academic year, subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability. We welcome undergraduates from all Faculties and MSc students to apply for this job. Interested students can submit your application via https://forms.gle/8FXtDJyk1C2BESQTA with:

on or before April 12, 2024 (Monday) . A confirmation email will be sent to you and an interview will be scheduled for shortlisted applicants.

Intro to Sequence Models
Do you want to know how ChatGPT works?
Interested in how Google Translate operates?
Many modern technologies, such as ChatGPT, Google Translate, AutoCorrect, and email filtering, are all built on top of sequence models! ᕦ(ò_óˇ)ᕤ
In this workshop series, we will introduce you to the theory and applications of sequence models. By learning how to use powerful machine learning models, you will eventually be able to create your own language models. (= ́∀`)人( ́∀`=)
In this first workshop, two basic sequence models: RNNs and LSTMs will be covered and you will have the skills to do language modelling, prediction problems, automated translations, and much more! (p_-)

title: Workshop by NestSpace: Create A Desktop Air Conditioner With Klipper (A Firmware for 3D Printer)
text:
Create A Desktop Air Conditioner With Klipper (A Firmware for 3D Printer)
Workshop offered by NestSpace
Date:
April 17 & 18, 2024 (Wednesday & Thursday)
Time:
6:30 – 8:00pm
Venue:
Makerspace A,
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Registration
The rising industry of 3D printing has not only transformed manufacturing but also gained immense importance in engineering careers. Among remarkable innovations in this field, Klipper firmware stands out as a key technology enabling fast and reliable 3D printing.
Recognizing the shared principles and mechanisms between 3D printing and other applications, we have chosen to host a workshop that focuses on utilizing the Klipper to create a desktop air conditioning unit. By delving into its architecture and applying it to this project, we aim to provide students with a valuable opportunity to equip themselves with the future of this industry. Through this workshop, we aspire to foster creativity, innovation, and practical skills that can be applied to a wide range of engineering endeavors.

Australia Study Tour
Get ready for an unforgettable experience on the Australia Study Tour, carefully curated to ignite your interest in advanced and sustainable technology. This exclusive tour is tailored for undergraduate students who are eager to explore cutting-edge technologies and discover innovative solutions for a more sustainable future.
From July 6 to 14, 2024, prepare to embark on an 9-day journey that will include visits to prestigious universities and centers, providing valuable insights and knowledge on the latest developments in innovation and sustainable technologies.

When there is an oversubscription, selection will be determined by drawing lots.
Announcement of lot drawing results:
Selected participants will be notified via email. Please kindly respond to the email and settle full payment on or before the before the designated deadline.
Notes to participants:
Participants are required to travel and stay with the team throughout the study tour, unless otherwise advised by tour leaders.
No separate inbound and / or outbound travel arrangements will be entertained
.
Participants are responsible for their own visa and travel document application or renewal, as well as any personal expenses incurred during the Australia study tour.
Participants are responsible for verifying whether they require an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) or a visitor visa for their travel and ensure a successful application before departure. Kindly note that the processing time for tourist visa application may take up to 33 days. Innovation Academy is not accountable for any losses incurred as a result of travel document-related issues leading to the inability to travel. Participants are advised to refer to the following webpage for detailed information regarding visa requirements for Australia:
https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing
.
Pre-trip briefing
All participants are required to attend the pre-trip briefing. It covers the details of the tour, reimbursement procedures and some key reminders. All students should have applied for or held a valid Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) or visitor visa by that time.
Payment Arrangement
Participants must settle full payments of airfare and hotel accommodation directly with the travel agency on or before the designated date (May 10, 2024). Reimbursement will ONLY be processed upon full attendance of all scheduled activities during this study tour, including pre-trip briefing and post-trip sharing, as well as the submission of a high-quality post-trip report.
Please note that no refund will be provided once the payment has been made. Innovation Academy does not handle any payment transactions in this regard.
Reimbursement Procedures
Participants will be able to reimburse up to a maximum 70% of total cost of eligible items at cost.
Participants submit reimbursement claim form together with all the necessary documents, including the boarding passes, to Innovation Academy.
Administration staff of Innovation Academy will process the application after receiving all the documents.
Finance and Enterprises Office of HKU will reimburse the eligible amount to participants according to their bank account information provided in the Student Information System (SIS) in HKU portal.
The whole process may take up to
three to four months
.
Insurance
Travel insurance provided by HKU:
Participants should note that the University only provides standard travel insurance coverage for overseas trips or study abroad programmes approved/arranged by the University. Before leaving Hong Kong, students are strongly advised to arrange their own travel insurance to better suit their needs, especially if they are planning to travel beyond the official programme period for personal leisure purpose. If students require additional or special insurance coverage, they will need to make their own personal arrangements at their own expense. The travel insurance coverage arranged by the University could not be extended to cover personal needs or leisure travelling arrangements. Participants should refer to Cedars webpage
(Click to learn more)
for more details.
Participants are advised to read through Travel Insurance Arrangement for Students
(Click to learn more)
and other related documents, such as 24/7 Global Travel Emergency Assistance Programme and the FAQ.
Post-trip Activities
Participants are required to fulfill the following post-trip activities:
Present in a sharing session, if any, for Inno Wing members and other Engineering students at HKU on July 26, 2024 (Friday).
Upon the completion of the study tour, participants are required to submit a reflection report with not less than 500 words, together with a minimum of 3 photo highlights by July 31, 2024 (Wednesday).

Participants must settle full payments of airfare and hotel accommodation directly with the travel agency on or before the designated date (May 10, 2024). Reimbursement will ONLY be processed upon full attendance of all scheduled activities during this study tour, including pre-trip briefing and post-trip sharing, as well as the submission of a high-quality post-trip report.
Please note that no refund will be provided once the payment has been made. Innovation Academy does not handle any payment transactions in this regard.
Participants submit reimbursement claim form together with all the necessary documents, including the boarding passes, to Innovation Academy.
Administration staff of Innovation Academy will process the application after receiving all the documents.
Finance and Enterprises Office of HKU will reimburse the eligible amount to participants according to their bank account information provided in the Student Information System (SIS) in HKU portal. The whole process may take up to three to four months .
Participants should note that the University only provides standard travel insurance coverage for overseas trips or study abroad programmes approved/arranged by the University. Before leaving Hong Kong, students are strongly advised to arrange their own travel insurance to better suit their needs, especially if they are planning to travel beyond the official programme period for personal leisure purpose. If students require additional or special insurance coverage, they will need to make their own personal arrangements at their own expense. The travel insurance coverage arranged by the University could not be extended to cover personal needs or leisure travelling arrangements. Participants should refer to Cedars webpage (Click to learn more) for more details.
Participants are advised to read through Travel Insurance Arrangement for Students (Click to learn more) and other related documents, such as 24/7 Global Travel Emergency Assistance Programme and the FAQ.
Present in a sharing session, if any, for Inno Wing members and other Engineering students at HKU on July 26, 2024 (Friday).
Upon the completion of the study tour, participants are required to submit a reflection report with not less than 500 words, together with a minimum of 3 photo highlights by July 31, 2024 (Wednesday).

title: Advanced Level Firmware Programming for Legged Robot
text:
Two-day Workshop on Advanced Level Firmware Programming for Legged Robot
Date:
July 30
and 31, 2024 (Tue and Wed)
Time:
2
:30 – 5:00pm
Venue:
Digital Learning Studio,
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Two-day Workshop on Advanced Level Firmware Programming for Legged Robot
Firmware is the software program in MCU (micro controller unit) to control the actuators such as servos and motors, and sensors of a robot. It is a challenge to develop a good firmware as MCU is not powerful as computer CPU. As MCU program runs in single thread model, programming techniques are required to efficiently coordinate each module (sensor or actuator) to avoid them from blocking each other.
In this two-day advanced level firmware programming workshop, topics like inverse kinematics, concurrent control of actuators, and object-oriented approach for robotics will be covered. To facilitate your learning, you will also be building your own legged robot, serving as a hands-on platform for programming, implementation, and control. Details of the workshop are as follows:

text:
Prototyping against Global Warming
Workshop offered by Designing solutions for construction workers against Global Warming (Hay-Koze)
Date:
July 21, 2024 (Sunday)
Time:
9:00am – 18:00pm
Venue:
Open Event Area, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One
Registration
The construction industry suffers the worst direct impacts of global warming: With 60% of construction workers in Hong Kong already having experienced symptoms of heat stroke. Hence, more effective cooling solutions are needed that are sensitive to the demands of the industry’s harsh environment.
To do so, skills and experience in prototyping is critical. Thus, we organize this workshop, including interactive lectures, hands-on production and final pitching, to educate students on topics such as problem finding, engineering principles, rapid iterative processes etc.; and consequently pass on our spirit of practical innovation. Thus, together, we can come to a solution for workers against global warming.

text:

Workshop 1

Registration for Generative AI Workshop: Exploring Multimodal RAG
Details
Get ready for an exciting workshop featuring the latest student projects in the field of Generative AI. Our Student Research Assistants have been working hard on interesting projects that are sure to pique your interest. Come join us to have a first-hand experience and discover the possibilities of these projects!
Interactive Showcase
All the three students research assistant projects will be featured at Makerspace A, with a designated booth for each project. An introductory PowerPoint presentation or short video clip will be prepared for each project and shown at their respective booth. Participants will have the opportunity to engage in hands-on experiences with all three projects. The brief descriptions of all three projects are shown below:
AIHA (AI Historian Assistant):
An AI-powered system designed to assist historians and general users in streamlining the retrieval and connection of scattered, multimodal historical sources they provide.
CLIC-Chat 3.0
: CLIC-Chat 3.0 extends our previous CLIC-Chat series by incorporating formal legal analysis and reasoning strategies.
SWITCH (Social Work Interactive Training CHatbot)
: SWITCH aims to develop a chatbot to roleplay users of social services with different backgrounds, facilitating the training of social workers.
Date: September 11, 2024 (Wednesday)
Time: 2:30 – 5:30pm
Venue: Makerspace A, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Registration for Interactive Showcase
Generative AI Workshop: Exploring Multimodal RAG
Join us for an engaging Generative AI workshop, focusing on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems and image retrieval for all levels of multimodal AI enthusiasts. Participants will grasp the foundational concepts of RAG and its multimodal extensions, exploring various methods and their practical applications.
Throughout the workshop, you will engage in theoretical discussions and hands-on activities, including text Optical Character Recognition (OCR), image extraction, and caption pairing with GPT-4o, to prepare your own datasets. You will also learn about vector search principles and embedding techniques, culminating in a complete pipeline demonstration comparing RAG to standard GPT. Join us to explore the exciting possibilities of multimodal AI, and elevate your skills to new heights!

and

By the end of the workshop, students are expected to:
Gain understanding of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Get familiarize with Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and the process of creating text & image-caption dataset.
Be able to perform vector search and embedding.
Successfully implement multimodal RAG.

Given the escalating global concerns about air quality, global warming, greenhouse gas emissions, and other related environmental issues, it has become crucial to explore new solutions and technologies aimed at addressing global environmental challenges. Microalgae, a type of plants that serves as a natural and sustainable method to reduce pollutants and generate biomass, plays a significant role in producing over 50 percent of the world’s oxygen.
Acknowledging the power and potential of microalgae, we have organized a workshop to introduce students to the latest advancements in microalgae technology and the fundamental mechanisms of microalgae. HKU iGEM team 2023 is a team of undergraduate students from different fields, aiming at building safe and sustainable projects that serve the public interest. Beginner ROS Workshop
ROS101 - A Beginner's Guide on Advanced Robots
Date:

Venue:
Digital Learning Studio,
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
What is Robot Operating System (
ROS)?
The Robot Operating System (ROS) (
https://www.ros.org/
) is a set of open-sourced software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms, and with powerful developer tools, ROS has what you need for your next robotics project. ROS is de facto industrial standard for developing system for robots. It is important to everyone who wants to work in the field of robotics.
Workshop Details
Robots are complex systems where sensors and motors work together. The Robot Operating System (ROS) facilitates seamless communication among these components. This workshop on ROS is tailored for beginners who are keen on advanced robotics, offering an overview of ROS fundamentals and showcasing how it integrates robotic components. By the end of the workshop, you will enhance your understanding of ROS and be able to modify your robots’ movement patterns.
This 2 hour workshop leads beginners to learn ROS framework:

Attention Is the Key From BCI to Futurism
Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology connects the human brain directly to machines, offering a unique way to study mind-technology interactions. By emphasizing BCI, we hope to inspire a futurism approach that bridges technological advancement and spiritual development. We’ve implemented BCI into drone technology, which AI will analyze the brainwave signals and gives an attention level. At certain attention level, the drone will fly. We hope our technology can help people to train their attention and spark interest in science concept behind our mind-controlling drone.
Digitoe
The Digitoe Smart Insoles project is partnered with HKU’s Orthopaedic Department at Queen Mary hospital, aiming to revolutionize foot health management through the integration of advanced sensor technology, mobile app feedback, and 3D printing. These smart insoles are designed to provide customized orthotic solutions that enhance foot health and alleviate pain, particularly for individuals with foot pain and improper posture.
EDVise
EDVise is a one-stop education consulting based on big data and AI algorithms to aid secondary school students in picking their future path. We found out that 80% of students today feel confused about their elective and JUPAS choices which will affect their future career choices, yet there are overwhelming amounts of resources in the market but none of them could cater individualsâ€TM needs and preferences. Introducing EDVise, which can solve this through providing personalized LLM and database consulting services. We are aiming to launch EDVise by next year, wholesaling at $1080HKD/year to local secondary schools with retail options.
FemiLab
Sudden start of menses ( induced by change in concentration of female sex hormones ) without any sign is a common issue that causes a lot of troubles. Unfortunately, commercially available female sex hormones tests do not cover menses and most of them require labs and technical experts. Meanwhile , there is no domestic test for gynecopathies such as breast cancer and PolyCystic Ovary Syndrome , which can be diagnosed by using female sex hormones as biomarkers . So, we design a biosensor with an app that allows users to perform female sex hormones test at home, which determine whether menstruation will commence on the day users conduct the test as well as the risk of sex hormones related gynecopathies. Users will be alarmed if abnormal female sex hormones levels are detected. Apart from these, users can find useful information of women health and earn tokens by regular usage of the device and sharing personal data in the app.
GingTrolley – Revolutionizing In-Flight Waste Management with Smart Sustainability
GingTrolley is a GreenTech solution revolutionizing in-flight waste management for airlines and aircraft manufacturers. This innovative waste trolley features a modular design with specialized compartments for immediate separation of waste streams like plastics, paper, and liquids, ensuring recyclables maintain purity. Integrated IoT sensors track waste volume and type in real-time, transmitting data to a cloud platform for analysis. This data-driven approach provides insights into passenger behavior and waste generation patterns, optimizing resource allocation and informing targeted sustainability initiatives.
Beyond efficient sorting, GingTrolley enables data-driven decision-making, helping airlines quantitatively track progress toward ESG goals, reduce waste disposal costs, and improve recycling rates. By combining smart technology with a practical, adaptable design, GingTrolley transforms cabin waste management from a challenge into an opportunity for environmental responsibility and operational efficiency.
SmartSocks: AI-Based Wearables for Feet Pronation Sensing and Customised Calf Massage
Hong Kong’s elderly population might face mobility challenges from untreated gait issues like pronation and supination—a problem affecting 35% of elderly globally. Left unchecked, these issues can cause chronic pain or disability, leading to costly surgeries or physiotherapy. Existing solutions to leg muscle relaxation—bulky massage devices or high-voltage wearables—are impractical for daily use due to their expense, weight, and reliance on frequent charging. Moreover, they do not personalise massage settings based on foot shape.
Therefore, we proposed SmartSocks which offer:
1. Lightweight, portable, and low-energy socks using soft robotics for targeted massage relief.
2. Smart sensors to track user steps and AI-powered app that personalises massage settings.
3. Comparable price with existing products
SmartSocks will provide customised leg massage based on sensor readings and AI analysis to assist elderly to walk more comfortably and help ease gait problems.
SolaraWeave- The Future of Sustainable Real Estate Fabrics
Traditional green technology is often costly and difficult for everyday people to adopt. As a social enterprise, we aim to break this barrier by introducing an affordable perovskite-based flexible solar shading system, priced at just HKD 200. This low-cost, high-efficiency solution makes sustainable cooling and renewable energy accessible for smart homes, curtains, windows, charging stations, camping gear, shopping areas, government spaces, outdoor events, construction sites, and even umbrellas.
By scaling adoption across Hong Kong, our technology can significantly reduce citywide heat, lower energy consumption, and cut carbon emissions, contributing to a more livable urban environment. Unlike traditional solar panels, our lightweight, flexible fabric is easy to install and integrate into daily life.
Furthermore, this innovation supports local businesses and creates new job opportunities in production, sales, and installation. Through affordability, accessibility, and awareness, we empower everyone to take part in Hong Kong’s sustainable future.
The Best Presenter
The pitching team who receives the highest total scores in the “Structure of Pitch” and “Delivery of Pitch” wins “The Best Presenter” award.

Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU

Advanced Level Firmware Programming for Legged Robot
Dive into the fascinating world of robotics firmware at our upcoming workshop! Firmware, the software program in the MCU (microcontroller unit) that commands the robot’s actuators and sensors, presents a unique challenge due to the limited processing power compared to a computer CPU. Developing efficient firmware for robots requires mastering programming techniques to coordinate various modules seamlessly, preventing them from interfering with each other.
In this workshop, topics like inverse kinematics, concurrent control of actuators, and object-oriented approach for robotics will be covered. You will also have a chance to control a legged robot, serving as a hands-on platform for programming, implementation, and control.

Selected participants will be notified via email. Please kindly respond to the email and settle full payment on or before the before the designated deadline.

.
Participants are responsible for their own visa and travel document application or renewal, as well as any personal expenses incurred during the tour.
Pre-trip briefing
All participants are required to attend the pre-trip briefing. It covers the details of the tour, reimbursement procedures and some key reminders.
Payment Arrangement
Participants must settle full payments of airfare and coach fare directly to the travel agency on or before the designated date. Reimbursement request will only be processed upon full attendance of all scheduled activities and submission of high-quality post-trip report and photos.
Please note that no refund will be provided once the payment has been made. Innovation Academy does not handle any payment transactions in this regard.
Reimbursement Procedures
Participants will be able to reimburse up to a maximum 70% of total cost of eligible items at cost.
Reimbursement request will only be processed upon full attendance of all scheduled activities and the submission of a high-quality post-trip reflection report (no less than 500 words), along with 3 photos highlights (not to be submitted in the same file of the report).
Participants submit reimbursement claim form together with all the necessary documents, including the
physical boarding passes
, to Innovation Academy.
Administration staff of Innovation Academy will process the application after receiving all the documents.
Finance and Enterprises Office of HKU will reimburse the eligible amount to participants according to their bank account information provided in the Student Information System (SIS) in HKU portal. The whole process may take up to three months.
Insurance
Travel insurance provided by HKU:
Participants should note that the University only provides standard travel insurance coverage for overseas trips or study abroad programmes approved/arranged by the University. Before leaving Hong Kong, students are strongly advised to arrange their own travel insurance to better suit their needs, especially if they are planning to travel beyond the official programme period for personal leisure purpose. If students require additional or special insurance coverage, they will need to make their own personal arrangements at their own expense. The travel insurance coverage arranged by the University could not be extended to cover personal needs or leisure travelling arrangements. Participants should refer to Cedars webpage
(Click to learn more)
for more details.
Participants are advised to read through Travel Insurance Arrangement for Students and other related documents, such as 24/7 Global Travel Emergency Assistance Programme and the FAQ.
Post-trip Activities
Participants are required to fulfill the following post-trip activities:
Present in a sharing session, if any, for Inno Wing members and other Engineering students at HKU on March 19, 2025 (Wednesday).
Upon the completion of the study tour, participants are required to submit a reflection report with not less than 500 words, together with a minimum of 3 good photos by March 31, 2025 (Monday)

In case of unavailability to attend any of the following activities, it is necessary to obtain prior approval from Innovation Academy. title: On the way to innovations in Archaeology: just see instead of imagining
text:
On the way to innovations in Archaeology: just see instead of imagining
Date:
January 22, 2025 (Wednesday)
Time:
3:30-5:00pm
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing, HKU
Archaeology and Augmented Reality have something in common, both are naturally three dimensional. Working on combining these two, our team suggests an innovative solution which sets the AR headsets to support the ongoing archaeological excavations for the first time ever. We equip an archaeologist with a head-mounted device which can place back the excavated and removed features from the trench. This option enables us to actually see things instead of imagining and memorizing them. The impact is significant to the understanding and interpretation of discovered material heritage. We invite you to try the “new archaeologist’s perspective” with augmented vision.

text:
Discover the Power of Microalgae
with bioreactor Stem Kit 2025
Workshop offered by WeGoALGAE
Session A: February 12, 2025 (Wednesday)
or

Time: 6:30 – 8:00pm
Venue: Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU

With rising global issues in air quality, global warming, greenhouse gas emissions and other related
environmental issues. New solutions and technologies that work to mitigate global environmental issues has always been an essential area to delve into. Microalgae is a plant that works as a natural and sustainable method to reduce pollutants and produce biomass. Microalgae provides more than 50 percent of the oxygen in this world.
Recognizing microalgae power and potential, we will expose you to the latest technology of microalgae and the basic mechanisms of microalgae. You will know all the basic and essential information about how a simple micro-algae photo-bioreactor works. You will have opportunities for microalgae implementation and work together for a greener world.

title: Workshop on Microcontrollers & APIs: Build Your Own WiFi-Enabled Mini TV
text:
Microcontrollers & APIs: Build Your Own WiFi-Enabled Mini TV
Date:
February 28 (Friday), 2025
Time:
2
:00 – 5:00pm
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Workshop Details
Imagine having a mini TV in your room that can always display the weather, a Google Calendar, or even your Notion databases. What if we told you that you could program one yourself?
In this beginner-friendly workshop, you’ll unlock these possibilities by learning about the ESP32 microcontroller, application programming interfaces (APIs), and how to integrate them by calling an API using the ESP32. By the end, you’ll have the skills to bring your creative ideas to life!
Date: February 28, 2025 (Friday)
Time: 2-5pm
Venue: Makerspace A,
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Class Size:
Maximum 15 participants
Register now
Learning Outcome
Gain an introductory understanding of microcontrollers and APIs.
Develop foundational knowledge of the Arduino IDE and its programming language.
Understand the integration of web APIs with microcontrollers and explore their potential applications.
Assemble and program a WiFi-enabled mini TV that uses APIs to display information such as the time, weather, a Google Calendar, or data from a Notion database.
Workshop Outline
Topics
Introduction (5 minutes)
Introduction to Microcontrollers (5 minutes)
Introduction to APIs (30 minutes)
Setting Up the Arduino IDE (20 minutes)
Connecting the ESP32 to WiFi (10 minutes)
APIs and JSON on the ESP32 (30 minutes)

text:
Soft Robotics: From Innovation to Commercialization
Speaker: Dr. Zheng Wang, Founder and CEO of Wisson Robotics

Time: 3:30-4:30pm

Details
Robotics has always been a popular branch in high-tech innovation, with
a history of
over 50 years
and
countless pinnacles from
cutting-edge
innovations to life-changing products and paradigm-shifting enterprises. Not so much for soft robots, however, with a much shorter past and a much quieter path to commercialization, despite being one of the most popular
specialty
research areas in robotics to-date. In this short dialog, we will pick a
consecutive
few concise but crucial topics from the journey our group has undertaken, over the past decade or so,
in
bring
ing
our take of soft robotics from its very infant phase of conceptual exploration all the way to product engineering and commercial application. We hope this could inspire some with an open heart for technical transfer and
those with a natural
appetit
e for curiosity into starting up a company to bring an idea to
realization
.
Date:
February 27, 2025 (Thursday)
Time:
3:30-4:30pm
Venue:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Speaker:
Dr. Zheng Wang, Founder and CEO of Wisson Robotics
All members of HKU community are welcome to join!
Register now!
About the speaker
Dr. Zheng Wang, Founder and CEO of Wisson Robotics
Dr Z. Wang
is the founder and CEO of Wisson Robotics, a global pioneer in general-purpose soft robots. By developing and deploying innovative soft robots with high safety, high performance, and low cost, Wisson aims to bring next-generation robotic products to the industry and households. Prior to founding Wisson, Dr Wang spent over a decade in academia, formerly a professor at the Institute of Robotics, Southern Univ. of Science and Technology, China, and an assistant professor at Department of Mechanical Engineering at HKU. Dr Wang holds a first degree in Automatic Control from Tsinghua University, China, PhD in Robotics from Technical University Munich, Germany, and served postdoc fellowships in NTU, Singapore and Harvard, USA.
As a technology leader, Wisdom specializes in Digital Twins, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, IoT, and AR/VR technologies. His deep understanding of these fields has been crucial in positioning Asia Infrastructure Solutions as a pioneer in digital technology implementation. His leadership style combines innovative thinking with practical execution, enabling the company to adapt and thrive in the rapidly evolving technological landscape.
Under his guidance, the company has successfully integrated emerging technologies into its core operations, setting new standards for digital innovation in the infrastructure sector. His vision continues to shape the company’s technological trajectory and its approach to solving complex construction challenges.

Date:

Venue:

Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Robot Arm Challenge 2025
What is Robot Operating System (
ROS)?
The Robot Operating System (ROS) (
https://www.ros.org/
) is a set of open-sourced software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms, and with powerful developer tools, ROS has what you need for your next robotics project. ROS is de facto industrial standard for developing system for robots. It is important to everyone who wants to work in the field of robotics.
Workshop Details
In this Robotic Manipulation workshop, you will develop a program to control a robot arm for automating the object sorting task!
Why object sorting?
To complete this task, the program must first
recognize
the object of interest in the camera view and then
coordinate
the robotic gripper to move over and grasp it. While seemingly simple, this challenge represents a fundamental problem in autonomous and intelligent robotic manipulation. If you’re new to this field or interested in enhancing the capabilities of robotic arms, this is a workshop you won’t want to miss

title: Sharing Session: Understanding Style in Computational Cinematography
text:
Understanding Style in Computational Cinematography
Speaker: Prof.
Marc Christie
– Associate Professor, University of Rennes and INRIA
Date: March 19, 2025 (Wednesday)
Time: 3:30-4:30pm
Venue:
Brainstorming Area, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, Hui Oi Chow Science Building, HKU
Register now!
Register now! (For non-HKU members)
Details
With recent breakthroughs in generative video techniques and more and more evolved feature extraction tools on video contents, there is a increasing expectation in being able to use and control stylistic dimensions of movies. Tasks such as film classification, style-driven generation, or transfer techniques from real videos to synthetic contents can all largely benefit from a better exploitation of film stylistic features. Yet in practice, our understanding of what style stands for in movies remains fairly limited and impedes our ability to properly formalize, extract and exploit such features. In this talk, we will introduce how state-of-the-art techniques approach the problem. We will share recent results on the topic, and open towards a more holistic vision that requires to understand style in strong correlation with more in-depth representations of movies such as discourse structures, intentionality, cognition and emotion.
Date: March 19, 2025 (Wednesday)
Time: 3:30-4:30pm
Venue: Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Speaker: Prof. Marc Christie – Associate Professor, University of Rennes and INRIA
All members of HKU community are welcome to join!
Register now!
About the speaker
Professor Marc Christie – Associate Professor, University of Rennes and INRIA
Marc Christie
is an Associate Professor at University of Rennes and INRIA. His research focuses on understanding the underlying visual and narrative constructs in movies, building computational models from these constructs, and applying the results to interactive or automated cinematography systems in real and virtual environments. His research finds applications in drone cinematography, in-game cinematics, sport broadcasting, and virtual production. He has been collaborating with game software companies such as Unreal and Unity, as well as with multiple VFX companies.

About Engineering Inno Show
Previous image
Next image
The Engineering Inno Show is a showcase carnival that celebrates innovative Engineering student projects at the end of every semester. Participating students will have the opportunity to expound on their inventive design, research and projects; harness timely and constructive feedback given by peers, teachers, industry experts and the public through knowledge exchange; and spin talent and ideas into innovative (re)inventions. There are many reasons why Engineering Inno Show is a unique concoction of its missions and vision. We offer a vibrant, inter/multi-disciplinary and hands-on learning platform for students to create their own impact, in and out of the classroom. The showcases also paint junior fellows a concrete picture of what constitutes an exemplary work and open pathways for them to look at Engineering through the lens of their senior cohorts. We believe that Engineering united with hands-on experience is essential. It is our vision to inspire a generation of intrepid explorers and committed collaborators. At Engineering Inno Show, we are transmitting knowledge and values through narrative. Whether it is communicated in layman’s terms or field-specific terminologies, we hope that the seeds of creative minds will germinate and thrive.

CLIC-Chat
CLIC-Chat is an innovative AI chat tool designed to provide reliable and up-to-date legal assistance with a focus on Hong Kong law. Unlike other chat tools, CLIC-Chat boasts a comprehensive HK knowledge database, ensuring accurate responses tailored to the local context. By leveraging the RAG technique, it guarantees trustworthy information while staying current with the latest legal developments. One of its standout features is the ability to ask valuable questions, akin to a skilled lawyer, to gather essential details from users’ stories. This enables CLIC-Chat to provide personalized legal guidance and suggestions, knowing precisely when to stop questioning and offer relevant insights. With CLIC-Chat, users can confidently navigate legal matters, receive accurate information, and make informed decisions.

SmartSocks: AI-Based Wearables for Feet Pronation Sensing and Customised Calf Massage
SmartSocks are lightweight, low-energy wearable socks designed to ease gait issues like pronation and supination, affecting 35% of the elderly. Using soft robotics and smart sensors, they provide gentle, targeted leg muscle relief tailored to each user’s walking pattern. Unlike bulky massage devices or high-voltage wearables, SmartSocks are practical for daily use—no heavy hardware, no frequent charging. An AI-powered app personalises massage settings based on foot shape and movement data. Offered at a competitive price, SmartSocks help elderly users walk more comfortably, reduce chronic pain risks, and improve mobility in a convenient, user-friendly way.

title: DIY Controller Workshop
text:
DIY Controller Workshop
Date:
April 11 (Friday) / April 16, 2025
Time:
6:
30 – 8:30pm / 4:30 – 6:30pm
Venue:
Makerspace A,
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Workshop Details
Matchbox is a DIY STEM kit we are developing at InnoWing to introduce people to 3D printing, electronics, and prototyping through a hands-on controller project made from upcycled keyboards! In this 2hr workshop, you will assemble your very own controller step by step to explore the various technologies that make it possible! You even get to keep the controller and play with your friends afterwards! We hope to use Matchbox to form an inviting bridge that opens up the fascinating tools and procedures available inside InnoWing to friends not from the engineering faculty! Come with us to make, learn, collaborate, and play with the Matchbox!
Date: April 11 (Friday) / April 16, 2025 (Wednesday)
Time: 6:30 – 8:30pm / 4:30 – 6:30pm
Venue: Makerspace A, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing One, HKU
Register now
Learning Outcome
Gain an introductory understanding of microcontrollers and APIs.
Develop foundational knowledge of the Arduino IDE and its programming language.
Understand the integration of web APIs with microcontrollers and explore their potential applications.
Assemble and program a WiFi-enabled mini TV that uses APIs to display information such as the time, weather, a Google Calendar, or data from a Notion database.
Workshop Outline
Topics
Introduction (5 minutes)
Introduction to Microcontrollers (5 minutes)
Introduction to APIs (30 minutes)
Setting Up the Arduino IDE (20 minutes)
Connecting the ESP32 to WiFi (10 minutes)
APIs and JSON on the ESP32 (30 minutes)
Creative Applications & Next Steps (5 minutes)
Q&A and Closing (15 minutes)

Workshop offered by Matchbox

Are you ready to dive into the art and science of game design? On April 25th (6:30 PM – 8:30 PM, InnoWing 1), Sky Chan, a talented game developer, will share his insights on “
A Systemic Approach to Analyze and Design Games
.”
In this interactive session, Sky will explore how to describe game design with a common language and uncover the connection between gameplay and emotions. Whether you’re a seasoned developer or just starting out, this talk is the perfect opportunity to learn how to create more impactful and meaningful gaming experiences.
What to Expect:
• Expert insights into systemic game design.
• Tips to bridge the gap between creativity and player connection.
• Opportunities to showcase your own game development projects!
Bring your projects to share and discuss with the community. Fireside Fridays are all about fostering collaboration, creativity, and passion for game development. Let’s build an inspiring space for innovation right here at HKU Innovation Academy!
Don’t miss out on this amazing opportunity to learn, network, and grow. Mark your calendars and join us for an evening of creativity and inspiration!

Venue:

Workshop Details
Co-presented by

and
HKU UAS Team
, this pilot workshop puts you at the forefront of Hong Kong’s emerging low-altitude economy (LAE). It introduces participants to Hong Kong’s drone ecosystem. Let’s dive into and explore the world of small unmanned aircraft (SUA).
What You’ll Learn:
– Key SUA regulations and safety practices in Hong Kong.
– Drone aerodynamics, flight controls, and the science behind flying.
– Hands-on experience with DJI Neo drones and the DJI Fly app.
Why Attend?
– Pilot DJI Neo drones first-hand
– Build confidence through guided flight simulations and VLOS (Visual Line of Sight) practice.
– Put your skills to the test with a fun and challenging obstacle course.

TRACES is an educational initiative dedicated to fostering inclusive learning through innovative programs including:

– Future Skills Workshops – Cutting-edge training in AI, drone technology, design thinking,
transdisciplinary innovation, etc.

Gain an introductory understanding of microcontrollers and APIs.

title: Study Tour – UK (Oct 2025)
text:
UK Study Tour
Date:
October 12 to 19, 2025
Highlights:
London x Manchester
Photo Gallery
UK Study Tour
This programme offers a comprehensive package including pre-departure meetings, post-tour workshops at HKU, and a 7-day tour focused on London, UK. The London portion will include visits to universities, companies, and museums to provide a thorough understanding of innovation and technology development in this leading European city.
Details
Date: October 12 to 19, 2025 (both dates inclusive)
Duration: 7 days 6 nights
Number of Participants:
a maximum of 16 Inno Wing members to be accompanied by staff/tutors/student research assistants (
When there is an oversubscription, selection will be determined by drawing lots.
)
Eligibility:
InnoWing Members are welcome to apply. Current Student Research Assistants will be given priority to join.
Support to student:
Innovation Academy will support each participant with a maximum of 70% reimbursement for the eligible items (round-trip airfare, hotel accommodation, local transportation). The expenses will be reimbursed at cost.
Designated transportations including coach and airfare (including 20kg luggage)
Coach fare
Hotel accommodation during the tour (twin room shared with another student)
*
Estimated trip cost: HK$25,000 (subject to change based on actual expenses). With a 70% reimbursement, your estimated out-of-pocket cost is HK$7,500 (also subject to change).
Tentative Itinerary
(Subject to change)
Person-in-charge must be informed if participants cannot show up at the any of the scheduled gather time of the study tour.
The person-in-charge reserves the right to modify the itinerary of the study tour based on the actual situation and time availability.
Application
Register Now
Deadline: 27 August 2025 (23:59) (WED)
Application requirement:
Complete the registration form by clicking the “
Register Now
” button.
When there is an oversubscription, selection will be determined by drawing lots.
Announcement of lot drawing results:
Selected participants will be notified via email. Please kindly respond to the email and settle full payment on or before the before the designated deadline.
Notes to participants:
Participants are required to travel and stay with the team throughout the study tour, unless otherwise advised by tour leaders.
No separate inbound and / or outbound travel arrangements will be entertained
.
Participants are responsible for their own visa and travel document application or renewal, as well as any personal expenses incurred during the tour.
Pre-trip briefing
All participants are required to attend the pre-trip briefing. It covers the details of the tour, reimbursement procedures and some key reminders.
Payment Arrangement
Participants must settle full payments of airfare and coach fare directly to the travel agency on or before the designated date. Reimbursement request will only be processed upon full attendance of all scheduled activities and submission of high-quality post-trip report and photos.
Please note that no refund will be provided once the payment has been made. Innovation Academy does not handle any payment transactions in this regard.
Reimbursement Procedures
Participants will be able to reimburse up to a maximum 70% of total cost of eligible items at cost.
Reimbursement request will only be processed upon full attendance of all scheduled activities and the submission of a high-quality post-trip reflection report (no less than 500 words), along with 3 photos highlights (not to be submitted in the same file of the report).
Participants submit reimbursement claim form together with all the necessary documents, including the
physical boarding passes
, to Innovation Academy.
Administration staff of Innovation Academy will process the application after receiving all the documents.
Finance and Enterprises Office of HKU will reimburse the eligible amount to participants according to their bank account information provided in the Student Information System (SIS) in HKU portal. The whole process may take up to three months.
Insurance
Travel insurance provided by HKU:
Participants should note that the University only provides standard travel insurance coverage for overseas trips or study abroad programmes approved/arranged by the University. Before leaving Hong Kong, students are strongly advised to arrange their own travel insurance to better suit their needs, especially if they are planning to travel beyond the official programme period for personal leisure purpose. If students require additional or special insurance coverage, they will need to make their own personal arrangements at their own expense. The travel insurance coverage arranged by the University could not be extended to cover personal needs or leisure travelling arrangements. Participants should refer to Cedars webpage
(Click to learn more)
for more details.
Participants are advised to read through Travel Insurance Arrangement for Students and other related documents, such as 24/7 Global Travel Emergency Assistance Programme and the FAQ.
Post-trip Activities
Participants are required to fulfill the following post-trip activities:
Deliver a presentation at a sharing session, if organized, for InnoWing members and other HKU Engineering students.
Submit a reflection report of at least 500 words, accompanied by a minimum of three high-quality photos after the study tour concludes.
LEARN MORE ABOUT the Post-trip Sharing Session
Important Timeline
Participants are required to fulfill all the following activities for reimbursement.
In case of unavailability to attend any of the following activities, it is necessary to obtain prior approval from Innovation Academy. Participants are required to submit a formal application to Innovation Academy, along with a valid explanation and supporting evidence, at least 48 hours before the start of the activity.
PREVIOUS Workshop
Workshop on “Indoor model airplane build and fly”
Next Workshop
2-day Beginner Workshop: Robot Control - Firmware
LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR OTHER WORKSHOPS 🙂
LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR OTHER Syudy Tour 🙂

What is Robot Operating System (
ROS)?
The Robot Operating System (ROS) (
https://www.ros.org/
) is a set of open-sourced software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms, and with powerful developer tools, ROS has what you need for your next robotics project. ROS is de facto industrial standard for developing system for robots. It is important to everyone who wants to work in the field of robotics.

About the speaker
Dr. Zheng Wang, Founder and CEO of Wisson Robotics
Dr Z. Wang
is the founder and CEO of Wisson Robotics, a global pioneer in general-purpose soft robots. By developing and deploying innovative soft robots with high safety, high performance, and low cost, Wisson aims to bring next-generation robotic products to the industry and households. Prior to founding Wisson, Dr Wang spent over a decade in academia, formerly a professor at the Institute of Robotics, Southern Univ. of Science and Technology, China, and an assistant professor at Department of Mechanical Engineering at HKU. Dr Wang holds a first degree in Automatic Control from Tsinghua University, China, PhD in Robotics from Technical University Munich, Germany, and served postdoc fellowships in NTU, Singapore and Harvard, USA.

title: WebGPU Workshop: Synthetic Animation & Simulation in the Browser
text:
WebGPU Workshop: Synthetic Animation & Simulation in the Browser
Date:
September 22, 2025 (Monday)
Time:
5:00am – 7:00pm
Venue:
Digital Learning Stuidio, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing
Register Now
Introduction
Join us for an exciting
WebGPU
programming workshop at The University of Hong Kong! This intensive session will introduce you to
traditional graphics programming
and
the power of general purpose GPU programming
which powers AI neural networks. WebGPU is a work in progress standard by the W3C to enable high-performance computing on the browser through native GPU access, it is one of the major tech behind WebAI – the tech that allows running AI models in your browser. By the end of the workshop, you’ll have created a dynamic and responsive particle effect graphics on a webpage.
This event is a perfect opportunity to enhance your programming skills and learn about graphics programming in the new academic year while connecting with fellow tech enthusiasts in the campus.
Date & Time

17:00 – 19:00
Location:
Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing, University of Hong Kong
Prerequisite:
HKU students
with basic programming understanding. You may bring your own laptop but make sure you have a
browser that supports WebGPU
, if you don’t have one, we will have computer provided to you.
What we’ll do:
Use JavaScript to build webpages that display dynamic graphical content using WebGPU API. We will create synthetic 2D graphics and responsive particle simulation by writing vertex, fragment, and compute shaders.
In the meantime,
we are looking for HKU students interested in joining our Google Developer Group
, where you will be able to meet other like-minded students and industry professionals across the GDG community!

title: From Theory to Hands on AI Model Training WITHOUT Coding
text:
From Theory to Hands on AI Model Training WITHOUT Coding
Date:
November 11, 2025 (Tuesday)
Time:
3
:30pm – 5:00pm
Venue:
Open Event Area, Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing
Register Now
Introduction
This is an interactive and educational workshop for AI beginners. Throughout this 1.5 hours, we would introduce the basics of AI solutions, guiding participants from zero knowledge to the ability to create functional AI models through hands-on model training. We leveraged our Nocodile AI platform for demonstration and hands-on experiences. Nocodile AI is a user-friendly platform with simplified AI training processes, intuitive interfaces, automated model training, and most importantly, no coding at all. These effectively break down the barriers that often deter newcomers from engaging with this transformative technology. We aim to not only let every participant taste the fun of creating AI solutions but also let them know that they should not limit their AI usage to ChatGPT only.
Learning Outcomes
Understand basic AI knowledge and the framework of developing AI solutions
Experience data collection, data annotation, model training, and model deployment using Nocodile AI platform
Integrate AI into products
Test the models in a real-life setting
